target.title: fix(amazon-bedrock-mantle): dedupe the IAM token-failure diagnostic per region (#67288)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #67288. On hosts with no usable AWS credentials (Raspberry Pi installs, default Docker images), the `amazon-bedrock-mantle` plugin attempts IAM bearer-token generation on every implicit-discovery call (every catalog refresh) and logs `[bedrock-mantle-discovery] Mantle IAM token generation unavailable` **every time** it fails. The user-visible symptom is continuous log noise on installs that never configured AWS.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix dedupes the failure diagnostic per region for the process lifetime instead of gating the IAM chain itself:

- `generateBearerTokenFromIam` keeps running the AWS default credential chain on every call — hosts that rely on late-arriving credentials (instance roles, IRSA, SSO) still start working the moment the chain succeeds, with no opt-in config.
- The `Mantle IAM token generation unavailable` debug line is emitted **at most once per region per process** (`iamTokenFailureLogged` set). A successful token generation for that region clears the marker, so a later regression logs again.

An earlier revision of this PR short-circuited discovery entirely when no AWS env creds were present; that approach was **abandoned after review** because it broke instance-role/IRSA/SSO hosts whose credentials are not visible in env vars. The current diff contains no credential gate and adds no config surface.

**Operator-observability tradeoff (explicit):** for a region that keeps failing, only the *first* failure's details are logged per process. If the underlying failure reason later changes (e.g. from "no credentials" to a network error) while generation keeps failing, the new details are not logged until a token generation succeeds for that region or the gateway process restarts. This trades per-request detail freshness for eliminating unbounded per-request log spam.

## User Impact

- Installs without AWS credentials see the diagnostic once per region instead of on every request.
- Hosts with working or late-arriving IAM chains are unaffected: token generation is still attempted every call.
- No config changes, no new keys, no behavior change for `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` users or explicit `discovery.enabled: false`.

## Evidence

Exact-head (c0e8c4d134b) regression run:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/amazon-bedrock-mantle/discovery.test.ts

 ✓ logs 'IAM token generation unavailable' at most once per region across repeated implicit-discovery calls (#67288)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  34 passed (34)
```

The regression drives the production `resolveImplicitMantleProvider` three times with a failing token provider and asserts, via a captured discovery-subsystem logger, that:
- the token provider factory ran on **all 3** calls (IAM-chain fallback semantics preserved — no short-circuit), and
- the `Mantle IAM token generation unavailable` diagnostic was emitted **exactly once**, with the expected `region` metadata — removing the dedupe guard fails the test.

Not yet supplied: redacted current-head runtime logs from a real credential-less host showing the single diagnostic across repeated catalog refreshes (the remaining reviewer ask).

Part of #67288.

target.title: fix(acp): ACP session startup fails when backend does not advertise thinking config
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103802 — Every `sessions_spawn(runtime: "acp")` against backends like OpenCode (which only advertise `mode, model` as supported config options) fails immediately with:

```
AcpRuntimeError: ACP backend "acpx" does not accept config key "thinking".: code=ACP_BACKEND_UNSUPPORTED_CONTROL
```

The ACP runtime resolves a thinking default (e.g., `"off"` for non-reasoning provider models) and injects it into spawn options. The backend rejects it because it doesn't advertise thinking as a supported config option. The caller cannot avoid this — passing no `thinking` in `sessions_spawn` does not prevent the injection.

## Why This Change Was Made

The root cause is in `resolveAcpSpawnRuntimeOptions` (`src/agents/acp-spawn.ts`): when no explicit thinking override is provided, the function falls through to `resolveThinkingDefault` and injects the auto-derived value into spawn options. This value then gets persisted and sent to the backend via `setConfigOption`, which rejects it.

The fix removes the auto-derivation fallback. If the caller doesn't provide an explicit thinking value, no thinking option is included in spawn options. This means:

- **Auto-derived defaults are never sent** — backends that don't advertise thinking work fine
- **Explicit user intent still fails visibly** — if someone passes `sessions_spawn(thinking: "high")` and the backend doesn't support it, the existing strict advertised-keys check in `applyManagerRuntimeControls` still throws `ACP_BACKEND_UNSUPPORTED_CONTROL`, same as before
- **No new code paths** — just removes the auto-injection, no prevention layer or safety net needed

## User Impact

ACP spawns targeting backends with limited config support (mode+model only) succeed instead of failing on init. Backends that support thinking/effort continue to work when explicitly requested. No behavior change for explicit thinking requests on non-supporting backends — they still fail visibly.

## Evidence

- 1 file changed, 2 insertions, 15 deletions
- Removes the auto-derivation block and the now-unused `resolveThinkingDefault` import
- All existing tests pass, `oxlint` reports 0 errors, 0 warnings

**Terminal evidence (commit d7bccfa):**

```
$ pnpm exec oxlint src/agents/acp-spawn.ts
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
```

**Live validation:** The same logic (stop injecting auto-derived thinking) was applied as a compiled JS patch to a running OpenClaw instance targeting an OpenCode ACP backend. Before the patch, every ACP spawn failed with `ACP_BACKEND_UNSUPPORTED_CONTROL`. After the patch, the thinking config option was never sent and session startup completed normally through a full first turn.

target.title: Refresh MCP OAuth auth-profile tokens
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Remote MCP servers can use OAuth credentials saved by `openclaw mcp login`, but CLI runners and Codex receive projected MCP client configuration instead of OpenClaw's embedded MCP transport. They therefore could not use or refresh those existing credentials. Operators had to copy an expiring bearer into config or create a separate auth-profile binding.

This PR makes the existing configuration work across embedded MCP, CLI runners, and local Codex app-server threads without migration:

```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "servers": {
      "docs": {
        "url": "https://mcp.example.com/mcp",
        "transport": "streamable-http",
        "auth": "oauth",
        "oauth": {
          "scope": "docs.read"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw already owns MCP OAuth login, credential storage, refresh, guarded HTTP policy, and embedded transport integration. External runtimes should consume that same credential owner rather than require a second configuration or static bearer rewrite.

`oauth.authProfileId` remains an optional alternate source for services already backed by a separate refresh-capable OpenClaw auth profile. Both sources now converge on one bearer-projection path, and only the current access token crosses the downstream runtime boundary.

## Summary

- Added optional `mcp.servers.*.oauth.authProfileId` schema/types/help/docs support.
- Added MCP-native OAuth as the default external-runtime token source for existing `auth: "oauth"` servers.
- Persisted access-token expiry metadata and refreshes pre-upgrade stores once when that metadata is absent.
- Serialized refresh per credential store with an in-process queue and cross-process file lock so rotating refresh tokens cannot race.
- Reused the guarded MCP HTTP fetch for refresh, preserving SSRF, TLS, proxy, and client-certificate policy.
- Kept explicit auth-profile selection as the higher-precedence optional source.
- Projected bearers through per-server environment variables for CLI runtimes and literal per-thread headers for local Codex app-server.
- Failed closed before resolving credentials for remote Codex app-server connections.
- Preserved Codex MCP tool filters and rotates a thread when the redacted bearer fingerprint changes.
- Replaced the broad auth-profile barrel import that caused the runtime-topology Madge cycle with leaf imports.
- Rebased the contributor branch onto current `main` at `b1e688c6577`.

## User Impact

Existing `auth: "oauth"` configurations created with `openclaw mcp login` now work in embedded MCP, CLI runners, and local Codex app-server without adding `oauth.authProfileId` or migrating config. Old credential stores are refreshed and enriched automatically on first external-runtime use.

Refresh tokens remain in OpenClaw's credential store. Remote Codex app-server connections do not receive locally owned OAuth credentials.

## Evidence

Focused MCP and Codex contract suite:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts \
  src/agents/bundle-mcp-config.test.ts \
  src/agents/cli-runner/bundle-mcp-codex.user-config.test.ts \
  src/agents/cli-runner/bundle-mcp.codex.test.ts \
  src/agents/cli-runner/bundle-mcp.test.ts \
  src/agents/cli-runner/bundle-mcp.user-config.test.ts \
  src/agents/mcp-auth-profile.test.ts \
  src/agents/mcp-http-fetch.test.ts \
  src/agents/mcp-oauth.test.ts \
  src/agents/mcp-transport-config.test.ts \
  src/agents/mcp-transport.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.user-mcp-servers.test.ts
```

Result: passed 3 Vitest shards / 144 tests.

Architecture:

```text

node --import tsx scripts/check-madge-import-cycles.ts
node scripts/check-deprecated-api-usage.mjs
node scripts/check-deprecated-jsdoc.mjs

## Real Behavior Proof

The PR's earlier localhost MCP proof demonstrated that an auth-profile-backed server receives only the current access bearer through both projected CLI config and same-origin embedded fetch, with stale and refresh tokens absent downstream.

The new MCP-native path is covered with an isolated real credential store plus the pinned MCP SDK auth boundary: fresh-token reuse, expired-token refresh and persistence, pre-upgrade store refresh, missing-login failure, guarded-fetch wiring, concurrent single-use refresh serialization, CLI projection, local Codex projection, and remote fail-closed behavior.

target.title: fix(google-meet): actually leave the Meet call in the browser on leave (#103386)
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #103386.

`openclaw googlemeet leave <session-id>` on the Chrome transports printed `left <session-id>` and marked the session `ended`, but only ran the registered stop hook (the realtime audio bridge; in transcribe mode nothing at all). No code path touched the meeting, so the browser participant kept sitting in the call — a ghost participant receiving audio/captions after the operator was told it left. Twilio sessions already end the real call via their stop hook, so the transports were inconsistent.

### Change

- `extensions/google-meet/src/transports/types.ts` + `chrome.ts`: join now persists the exact tab identity on the session — `browserTargetId` plus `browserTabOpenedByPlugin` (opened via `/tabs/open` vs adopted via `reuseExistingTab`). `openMeetWithBrowserRequest` returns it through both the local and node launch paths.
- `chrome.ts`: new `leaveChromeMeet` / `leaveChromeMeetOnNode` (shared `leaveMeetWithBrowserRequest` core). Leave acts on the persisted target only: verifies the tab still exists (already-closed is a clean no-op), clicks Meet's **Leave call** button via browser evaluate (reliable now that tabs are pinned to `?hl=en`), then closes the tab **only when the plugin opened it** — reused user-owned tabs get the click but stay open. Failures degrade to session notes instead of throwing.
- `extensions/google-meet/src/runtime.ts`: `leave()` calls the browser leave for `chrome`/`chrome-node` sessions and records the outcome in session notes. Guards:
  - sessions with no tracked tab (e.g. `chrome.launch: false`, or browser control never returned a targetId) get an explicit note instead of a guessy URL match;
  - the internal tab-reassignment path in `join()` passes `keepBrowserTab: true` so agent handoff keeps the in-call tab and avoids lobby re-admission;
  - the shared-tab guard compares the persisted `browserTargetId` + node context — same meeting URL in a different browser/node no longer suppresses departure.
- `docs/plugins/google-meet.md`: `leave` row now documents the Chrome-transport behavior.

### Review follow-up (b95168f8ece)

All three ClawSweeper P1 findings addressed: leave no longer rediscovers tabs by URL (persisted `targetId` from join), never closes tabs it did not open (opened-vs-reused ownership tracked), and the shared-tab guard is scoped to the actual target + browser context. A reused-tab regression test now covers the default `reuseExistingTab: true` path end to end.

## Verification

- `pnpm test extensions/google-meet` — 17 files, 209 tests passed. New/updated regressions: plugin-opened tab leave (click + close on the exact persisted target), reused user-owned tab leave (click, `DELETE` throws in the mock if attempted, tab stays open), already-closed tab leave (clean note, no `DELETE`), and a vm test that the leave script clicks only an enabled Leave call button.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions && pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — clean.
- oxfmt / oxlint on touched files — clean.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: `googlemeet leave` leaves the browser participant in the Google Meet call on chrome/chrome-node transports while reporting `left`.
Real environment tested: No live Google Meet call was run; behavior is proven at the browser-proxy request boundary with the plugin's existing stubbed-gateway test harness (same harness the join/status paths use), covering opened, reused, and already-closed tab lifecycles.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `pnpm test extensions/google-meet` and `pnpm test extensions/google-meet/index.test.ts`.
Evidence after fix: "leaves the Meet call in the browser when a chrome session leaves" asserts the `/act` evaluate carries the leave-click script against the persisted join target and that `DELETE /tabs/local-meet-tab` is issued; "keeps a reused Meet tab open on leave" asserts the same click against an adopted pre-existing tab with a mock that throws on any `DELETE`.
Observed result after fix: 209/209 tests pass; leave issues real browser actions scoped to the session's own tab and records an explanatory note in every fallback path.
What was not tested: A live Meet meeting (real Chrome, real Google account) and the chrome-node transport against a physical node; both share `leaveMeetWithBrowserRequest`, which is covered by the harness. Live-call proof of actual participant departure is pending a real Meet setup.

target.title: fix(memory): session sync deletes and re-embeds every indexed chunk as transcripts grow
target.body:
Closes #40919
Related: #59577 #75179 (earlier attempts by the same author, superseded — see "Why" below)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with long-running conversations would see growing CPU/disk spikes and sync latency because every session-memory sync deletes and re-inserts **every** indexed chunk of the transcript, even though a growing session only appends content. `writeChunks` clears all `memory_index_chunks`, FTS, and vector rows for the file and rewrites them from scratch on each dirty sync, so the per-sync cost grows linearly with session length (#40919).

## Why This Change Was Made

Session sync now diffs the freshly chunked transcript against the indexed rows using the **existing content-addressed chunk id** (`hash(source:path:startLine:endLine:chunkHash:model)`): unchanged chunks are left completely untouched, only stale ids are deleted, and only new chunks are embedded and inserted (one immediate transaction, embeddings computed before any deletion so a failure cannot leave the index partially pruned).

Key design decisions:

- **The index itself is the manifest** — no schema changes, no new offset/high-water-mark state, no config surface. Because chunking is deterministic and transcripts are append-mostly, all but the trailing chunk keep their ids across syncs; compaction/model switches change ids and naturally converge to a full replace.
- **Safe fallbacks**: the delta planner falls back to the existing full clear-and-rewrite path on first index, duplicate chunk ids, or when derived FTS/vector rows don't match the chunk rows **id-exactly** (e.g. FTS/vector enabled after rows were written, drift from a degraded write, old-model FTS leftovers) — the full rewrite is what heals those states today, and this preserves that. A chunk persisted with an empty embedding (partial provider failure) is re-embedded rather than frozen as "unchanged". After a clean write the parity result is remembered per file (process-local), so steady-state syncs skip the probes; any degraded write forces a re-probe.
- **Authoritative write transaction (addresses ClawSweeper's P1)**: the plan passes the ids of rows to *keep*; stale ids are derived from the **live rows inside `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`** (`live − (keep ∪ inserted)`), so a concurrent writer's commit between plan and write cannot leave rows the delete list doesn't know about. If a racing writer removed rows the plan meant to keep (they can't be restored — their embeddings were skipped), the file record is deliberately **not** updated, so the file stays hash-dirty and the next sync replans from live rows and re-embeds what's missing. Both races have deterministic regression tests.
- **Idempotent under concurrent writers**: chunk inserts upsert, vector writes replace, and the delta pre-deletes FTS rows for the ids it inserts (FTS5 has no ON CONFLICT), so a gateway sync racing a CLI sync cannot duplicate FTS rows.
- **Batching preserved**: the diff happens before embedding, so the source-wide batch path (#89138) submits only new chunks; the hash-keyed embedding cache still applies on top.
- **Scope boundary**: only `source === "sessions"` uses the delta path. Memory files keep the full rewrite. Chunking, ids, schema, and search behavior are unchanged.

Why this supersedes #59577/#75179: those branches targeted the legacy `chunks` table (pre-`memory_index_*` schema), added offset columns (schema migration risk), didn't integrate with source-wide batching, and lacked behavior proof. This implementation targets current `main`, needs no migration, and includes measurements.

## User Impact

Long conversations no longer make session-memory sync progressively heavier: steady-state syncs touch only the few chunks that actually changed. No behavior change to search results, citations, or configuration — the final index state is identical to a full rewrite.

## Evidence

**Real CLI behavior proof** (requested by ClawSweeper): real `openclaw memory index` runs from this branch against an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, sessions source with `experimental.sessionMemory: true`, hybrid/FTS on, FTS-only provider (`provider: "none"`), on a 100-turn session transcript (200 JSONL lines → 20 chunks). Terminal output (paths redacted):

```text
$ openclaw memory index --verbose        # run 1: initial index of the 100-turn transcript
Memory Index (main)
Provider: none (requested: none)
Sources: sessions (<STATE_DIR>/agents/main/sessions/*.jsonl)
[memory] sync: indexing session files
Memory index updated (main).

# append turns 101-102 to session-longrun.jsonl, then:
$ openclaw memory index --verbose        # run 2: incremental
[memory] sync: indexing session files
[memory] sync: incremental session chunk delta
Memory index updated (main).

# append turns 103-104, then:
$ openclaw memory index --verbose        # run 3: steady state
[memory] sync: indexing session files
[memory] sync: incremental session chunk delta
Memory index updated (main).
```

Structured debug log lines (`logging.level: debug`, from the file log, redacted):

```text
run 2: "memory sync: incremental session chunk delta" {"path":"sessions/main/session-longrun.jsonl","new":1,"stale":1,"kept":19}
run 3: "memory sync: incremental session chunk delta" {"path":"sessions/main/session-longrun.jsonl","new":2,"stale":1,"kept":19}
```

Row-churn accounting from the agent SQLite (`memory_index_state.revision` increments on every chunk/source row insert/update/delete):

| Run | Chunks | FTS rows | Revision | Row mutations this sync |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (initial index) | 20 | 20 | 21 | 21 (expected: full build) |
| 2 (append 2 turns) | 20 | 20 | 24 | **3** (1 stale delete + 1 insert + 1 record) |
| 3 (append 2 turns) | 21 | 21 | 28 | **4** (1 stale delete + 2 inserts + 1 record) |

On main, runs 2 and 3 would each be ~41 mutations (delete all 20 + reinsert + record) plus a full FTS rewrite; 19 of 20 chunks were never touched (`kept:19`).

**Focused tests** (`extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager.session-chunk-delta.test.ts`, 7 tests, real sqlite + FTS):
- appending turns re-embeds only trailing/new chunks; unchanged rows keep id + `updated_at` (no delete-reinsert), FTS row count stays in lockstep
- compacted/rewritten transcript falls back to a clean rebuild with no stale rows
- embedding failure mid-delta leaves the previous index fully intact; next sync converges
- **race: rows committed by a concurrent writer between plan and write are still deleted** (stale ids derived from live rows inside the transaction)
- **race: when a concurrent writer removed rows the plan kept, the file record is deferred and the next sync converges**
- a chunk persisted with an empty embedding is re-embedded on the next sync instead of being frozen
- FTS-only mode (no provider) applies deltas too

target.title: fix(plugins): honor empty document extractor scope
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Document extractor resolution treated an explicit empty plugin scope as if no scope was provided. With `onlyPluginIds: []`, document extractor discovery could still expand bundled extractor owners instead of returning no extractors.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin scope helper already preserves the difference between an omitted scope and an explicitly empty scope. This change moves the fix to the shared bundled manifest contract resolver and uses the same helper for the document extractor allowlist branch, so both bundled contract discovery and document extractor resolution share one scope contract.

## User Impact

Callers that intentionally pass an empty document extractor scope now get no extractors, including when an operator plugin allowlist is present. Omitted scope still discovers enabled bundled document extractors normally.

## Evidence

- Changed `src/plugins/bundled-manifest-contract-plugins.ts` to use `createPluginIdScopeSet` instead of a local helper that collapsed empty scopes.
- Changed `src/plugins/document-extractors.runtime.ts` to use the same scope helper for the operator allowlist branch.
- Added `src/plugins/bundled-manifest-contract-plugins.test.ts` proving omitted scope still returns a bundled contract owner while `onlyPluginIds: []` returns none.
- Kept document extractor regression coverage for empty scope with and without an operator allowlist.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/bundled-manifest-contract-plugins.test.ts src/plugins/document-extractors.runtime.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed: 2 files / 6 tests.
- `corepack pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundled-manifest-contract-plugins.ts src/plugins/bundled-manifest-contract-plugins.test.ts src/plugins/document-extractors.runtime.ts src/plugins/document-extractors.runtime.test.ts` passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/plugins/bundled-manifest-contract-plugins.ts src/plugins/bundled-manifest-contract-plugins.test.ts src/plugins/document-extractors.runtime.ts src/plugins/document-extractors.runtime.test.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check upstream/main..HEAD` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Controlled runtime proof: `node --import tsx - <<'EOF' ...` invoked the real document extractor resolver without test mocks.

## Proof

target.title: fix(mattermost): backfill thread history from server when in-memory window is empty
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Mattermost users replying in an existing thread could lose earlier thread context after the OpenClaw monitor restarted or the agent session was reset.

Fixes #93204

## Why This Change Was Made

The Mattermost monitor now backfills a cold local thread-history window from the Mattermost thread endpoint after inbound admission gates pass. The backfill marker is keyed by the stored thread `sessionId`, not the stable route session key, so a real `/new` or session reset in a thread gets its own recovery fetch while same-session follow-ups avoid repeated server fetches.

When the first cold turn has no stored thread session entry yet, the monitor records a pending backfill marker and adopts it once `recordInboundSessionMeta` creates the stored session id. That keeps the marker stable for same-session follow-ups and failed-fetch no-retry, without blocking a later real session-id rotation.

Recovery is now bounded on both axes flagged in review:

- **Thread response size.** `fetchMattermostThreadPosts` requests only the newest `historyLimit + 1` posts via `?per_page=<limit>&direction=up`, then restores ascending chronological order. `GET /posts/{id}/thread` returns the entire thread by default (Mattermost `per_page=0`), so an unbounded thread would otherwise allocate and parse on the inbound path.
- **Marker lifecycle.** Backfill tracking uses one marker per thread history key (`Map<historyKey, sessionId>`) instead of a process-lifetime `Set` of `historyKey:session` compound keys. Marker memory and lookup cost stay bounded to live threads instead of accumulating an entry per session rotation and scanning the whole set on each candidate. The stored session id is read only after the admission gates, so dropped pre-admission posts never touch the session store.

## User Impact

Mattermost thread replies keep useful prior context after restart or `/new`, without repeated thread-history requests, unbounded thread fetches, or unbounded per-session marker growth on long-lived monitors.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/client.test.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.test.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.inbound-system-event.test.ts`: **3 files, 112 passed**. Covers stored thread `sessionId` rotation, same-session no-refetch, failed-fetch no-retry, dropped pre-admission posts, adopt-pending-marker without blocking later rotation, and the initially-missing session entry path.
- Bounded fetch asserted (`client.test.ts`): a limited call issues `?per_page=2&direction=up` and re-sorts ascending so callers still build history oldest-first.
- Bounded marker asserted (`monitor.test.ts`): the backfill requests `historyLimit + 1`, and `threadBackfillMarkers.get(historyKey)` carries the current session marker across the rotation / no-refetch / no-retry / adopt paths.
- Rebased onto latest `origin/main` (resolved additive test-mock conflicts in `monitor.inbound-system-event.test.ts`; branch is now 0 behind).

Live proof: local Docker Mattermost Team Edition 10.11.21 at `http://localhost:8065`, with tokens and Mattermost ids redacted. The proof used real Mattermost REST auth, posts, and `/api/v4/posts/<root>/thread` through `monitorMattermostProvider`; a fake websocket only injected `posted` events into the monitor. The route/thread session key stayed stable while the stored thread `sessionId` rotated. Cold start included prior root/thread context, same-session server-only context stayed absent, and stored-thread-session reset included new server-only prior context:

```json
{
  "mattermost": "10.11.21 local Docker, token/id redacted",
  "routeSessionKey": "stable, redacted",
  "threadSessionKey": "stable, redacted",
  "threadSessionKeyStable": true,
  "storedThreadSessionIds": [
    "stored-session-before-reset",
    "stored-session-after-reset"
  ],
  "dispatchCount": 3,
  "firstColdStartContainsPriorThreadContext": true,
  "firstColdStartContainsRootContext": true,
  "sameSessionSkippedServerOnlyContext": true,
  "storedThreadSessionIdResetContainsNewPriorContext": true
}
```

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #67288. On hosts with no usable AWS credentials (Raspberry Pi installs, default Docker images), the `amazon-bedrock-mantle` plugin attempts IAM bearer-token generation on every implicit-discovery call (every catalog refresh) and logs `[bedrock-mantle-discovery] Mantle IAM token generation unavailable` **every time** it fails. The user-visible symptom is continuous log noise on installs that never configured AWS.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix dedupes the failure diagnostic per region for the process lifetime instead of gating the IAM chain itself:

- `generateBearerTokenFromIam` keeps running the AWS default credential chain on every call — hosts that rely on late-arriving credentials (instance roles, IRSA, SSO) still start working the moment the chain succeeds, with no opt-in config.
- The `Mantle IAM token generation unavailable` debug line is emitted **at most once per region per process** (`iamTokenFailureLogged` set). A successful token generation for that region clears the marker, so a later regression logs again.

An earlier revision of this PR short-circuited discovery entirely when no AWS env creds were present; that approach was **abandoned after review** because it broke instance-role/IRSA/SSO hosts whose credentials are not visible in env vars. The current diff contains no credential gate and adds no config surface.

**Operator-observability tradeoff (explicit):** for a region that keeps failing, only the *first* failure's details are logged per process. If the underlying failure reason later changes (e.g. from "no credentials" to a network error) while generation keeps failing, the new details are not logged until a token generation succeeds for that region or the gateway process restarts. This trades per-request detail freshness for eliminating unbounded per-request log spam.

## User Impact

- Installs without AWS credentials see the diagnostic once per region instead of on every request.
- Hosts with working or late-arriving IAM chains are unaffected: token generation is still attempted every call.
- No config changes, no new keys, no behavior change for `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` users or explicit `discovery.enabled: false`.

## Evidence

Exact-head (c0e8c4d134b) regression run:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/amazon-bedrock-mantle/discovery.test.ts

 ✓ logs 'IAM token generation unavailable' at most once per region across repeated implicit-discovery calls (#67288)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  34 passed (34)
```

The regression drives the production `resolveImplicitMantleProvider` three times with a failing token provider and asserts, via a captured discovery-subsystem logger, that:
- the token provider factory ran on **all 3** calls (IAM-chain fallback semantics preserved — no short-circuit), and
- the `Mantle IAM token generation unavailable` diagnostic was emitted **exactly once**, with the expected `region` metadata — removing the dedupe guard fails the test.

Not yet supplied: redacted current-head runtime logs from a real credential-less host showing the single diagnostic across repeated catalog refreshes (the remaining reviewer ask).

Part of #67288.

target.title: fix(auth): refresh OAuth tokens inside pre-expiry margin
target.body:
Fixes #103846

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators with Anthropic OAuth credentials would silently skip token refresh while still inside the intended pre-expiry refresh window: the auth manager decided a refresh was required, took the refresh lock, then the shared OAuth helper returned the unchanged credential without calling the provider token endpoint.

## Why This Change Was Made

`getOAuthApiKey` only refreshed after the stored `expires` timestamp had fully elapsed, while `hasUsableOAuthCredential` treats credentials as unusable once they are within the shared 5-minute margin. This change makes `getOAuthApiKey` use the same pre-expiry margin by default (with optional override/disable) so manager-driven refresh actually attempts a provider refresh instead of no-opping.

## User Impact

Anthropic (and other built-in OAuth providers routed through `getOAuthApiKey`) refresh earlier and more reliably near expiry, reducing silent keep-using-stale-token windows that the auth manager already intended to close.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass)

Commands:
```text
# Before fix (repro on origin/main): manager needs refresh, but getOAuthApiKey no-ops
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/llm/utils/oauth/get-oauth-api-key.margin.repro.test.ts
# OBSERVED
# {"managerSaysNeedsRefresh":true,"networkRefreshCallWasMade":false,"returnedAccessSameAsStale":true,"returnedExpiresSameAsStale":true}

# After fix
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/llm/utils/oauth/get-oauth-api-key.margin.test.ts
# 5 tests passed
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/llm/utils/oauth/anthropic.test.ts
# 12 tests passed
./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/llm/utils/oauth/index.ts src/llm/utils/oauth/get-oauth-api-key.margin.test.ts
./node_modules/.bin/oxlint src/llm/utils/oauth/index.ts src/llm/utils/oauth/get-oauth-api-key.margin.test.ts
```

Focused margin suite result after patch:
```text
 ✓ |unit| src/llm/utils/oauth/get-oauth-api-key.margin.test.ts (5 tests)
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: When an Anthropic OAuth credential is inside the 5-minute pre-expiry margin, manager-driven refresh must call the provider refresh path and persist updated credentials (not silently return the stale credential).
- Environment: local macOS openclaw checkout on `fix/103846-oauth-refresh-margin`, Node via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (provider token endpoint stubbed; manager/lock/store paths real).
- Current-main contrast: With `refreshMarginMs: 0` (main-era helper contract), the same inside-margin credential returns unchanged access and never calls `refreshToken` (`mainEraNoOpAccess: "stale-access-margin"`). After this patch, the default-margin helper + manager path refreshes and persists.
- Exact steps after patch:
  1. Seed auth profile store with Anthropic OAuth `expires = now + 4m` (inside `DEFAULT_OAUTH_REFRESH_MARGIN_MS`).
  2. Assert `hasUsableOAuthCredential` → false (manager needs refresh).
  3. Control: `getOAuthApiKey(..., { refreshMarginMs: 0 })` → no network refresh, stale access returned.
  4. Run `createOAuthManager.resolveOAuthAccess` with production-shaped `refreshCredential` that calls real `getOAuthApiKey`.
  5. Assert provider `refreshToken` called once, API key is fresh, and reloaded store has new access/refresh/expires.
- Command:
```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-refresh-margin.manager-path.proof.test.ts
# ✓ 1 passed
# [oauth-margin-proof] result: {
#   "managerNeedsRefresh": true,
#   "networkRefreshCallWasMade": true,
#   "returnedApiKey": "fresh-access-margin",
#   "mainEraNoOpAccess": "stale-access-margin",
#   "persistedAccess": "fresh-access-margin",
#   "marginMs": 300000
# }
```
- Focused helper suite (still green):
```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/llm/utils/oauth/get-oauth-api-key.margin.test.ts
# 5 tests passed
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/llm/utils/oauth/anthropic.test.ts
# 12 tests passed
```
- Evidence after fix: manager-path proof logs `networkRefreshCallWasMade: true` and `persistedAccess: "fresh-access-margin"`; main-era control remains a no-op.
- Control check: `refreshMarginMs: 0` / outside-margin cases still skip refresh; fully elapsed expiry still refreshes; constant alignment test keeps helper margin == auth-profiles default.
- Observed result after fix: inside-margin manager refresh is no longer a silent no-op; credentials are refreshed and persisted under the real lock/store path.
- What was not tested: Live Anthropic token endpoint exchange over the public network; multi-agent cross-store mirror races (covered by sibling oauth.mirror-refresh tests).


## AI disclosure

This fix was authored with AI assistance (Grok). Human operator reviewed selection and submission under the auto contributor pipeline. Proof commands and observed outputs above are from real local runs on this host.

target.title: fix(usage): reclaim refresh locks leaked by the current process (#103910)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw gateway usage-cost` can get stuck with `cacheStatus.status: "refreshing"` indefinitely: `pendingFiles` never drain, `refreshedAt` goes stale, and repeated queries hours apart return byte-identical responses frozen at an old `updatedAt`. Root cause: usage-cost refreshes serialize on a pid-stamped lock file (`.usage-cost-cache.json.lock`) whose staleness check trusts **pid-liveness alone** (`isUsageCostCacheRefreshRunning` → `isProcessRunning(lock.pid)`). A lock leaked by the gateway's **own process** — e.g. an in-process SIGUSR1 restart abandoning a mid-refresh promise before its `finally` releases, exactly the long-lived systemd deployment in the report — holds a pid that stays alive for the process's whole lifetime, so every subsequent `refreshCostUsageCacheForPath` returns `"busy"` forever while the background queue keeps re-scheduling. Fixes #103910.

## Why This Change Was Made

Track lock tokens held by this process in a module-level in-memory set: `acquire` registers the token, `release` removes it. The staleness check now reclaims a lock stamped with **our own pid whose token has no live in-process holder** (including tokenless legacy locks) — that lock cannot represent a running refresh in this process. Cross-process locks keep the existing pid-liveness semantics unchanged; genuinely running refreshes (registered token) are still respected. No new options or public surface.

## User Impact

`usage-cost` recovers by itself after a leaked lock instead of serving an aging snapshot that permanently claims to be "refreshing" — the failure mode that let a $1k+/month spend go unnoticed in the linked reports.

## Evidence

Discriminating regression test — forge a lock with `pid: process.pid` and an unregistered token (the leaked-self-lock state), then request a refresh:

```
main:     AssertionError: expected 'busy' to be 'refreshed'   ← stuck forever
this PR:  70/70 passed — lock reclaimed, refresh proceeds
```

The pre-existing "respects live usage cache locks even when they are old" test was retargeted to a genuinely foreign live pid (`process.ppid`), preserving its original intent under the new same-pid contract. Full suite `session-cost-usage.test.ts` 70/70; `tsgo:core` 0 errors; `oxfmt`/`oxlint` clean.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Android app had a read-only Skills settings surface while the Control UI already supports a fuller skills-management workflow. Android users could inspect Gateway skill status, but they could not search installed skills, turn skills on or off, or install skills from ClawHub from the app.

This PR adds those management paths while keeping ClawHub identity resolution, trust evaluation, and final installation enforcement on the Gateway.

## Summary

- Extend Android Skills settings with installed-skill search, Web-aligned status filters, and per-skill enable/disable through `skills.update`.
- Add ClawHub registry search and install through `skills.search`, `skills.detail`, and `skills.install`.
- Add a fail-closed Android pre-install review dialog showing the resolved skill identity, exact version, publisher, ClawHub audit result, findings, and audit URL.
- Add the dedicated admin-scoped `skills.securityReview` RPC for one exact ClawHub release.
- Preserve final Gateway trust enforcement: Android can acknowledge a non-blocked review-required release only from the review dialog; a malicious/blocked release cannot expose an install action and remains rejected by `skills.install`.
- Parse `blockedByAgentFilter` for accurate Android status and update the Android README/i18n inventory.

## Web UI Reference Checked

Reviewed the existing Control UI skills implementation in:

- `ui/src/pages/skills/view.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/skills/skills-page.ts`
- `ui/src/lib/skills/index.ts`

Android mirrors the relevant workflows: installed-skill filtering/status grouping, global enable/disable, ClawHub search/install, and risk-aware install confirmation.

## Gateway/API Contract

`skills.securityReview` is a separate `operator.admin` RPC. It is not an `items[]` extension to `skills.securityVerdicts`.

- Request: one required `slug`, one required exact `version`, and optional `ownerHandle`; additional properties are rejected.
- Registry boundary: the Gateway resolves the configured default ClawHub registry. The client cannot provide an arbitrary registry URL.
- Lookup scope: the handler requests only that exact release and does not scan installed skills.
- Identity binding: the returned requested slug/version and resolved slug/version must all match. When `ownerHandle` is supplied, the returned publisher must also match.
- Response: the existing sanitized `openclaw.skills.security-verdicts.v1` envelope with one reviewed item, including the derived `disposition` used by Android.
- Failure behavior: missing, unavailable, or identity-mismatched verdicts fail the RPC. Android treats a missing/invalid review as unavailable and keeps installation disabled.
- Final enforcement: `skills.install` independently re-evaluates Gateway trust policy. The pre-install review does not authorize or bypass installation.

`skills.securityVerdicts` remains the passive installed-skill verdict collection method and is unchanged by this contract.

Current PR head:

- Branch: `snowzlmbot/openclaw:android-skills-management`

- Proof commit: `478cf6e00417052330babacef35c5fd017ffd11b`

- App launch: normal Android launcher, screenshot mode disabled

The artifact's `latest-head.txt` records all three exact-head values as the same commit:

- `github_api_pr_head=8cc6ce03f8b14f45241de6eb4c42f1b68a651e90`
- `expected_pr_head=8cc6ce03f8b14f45241de6eb4c42f1b68a651e90`

The proof starts a temporary Gateway from that exact checkout and drives the production Android path against a deterministic ClawHub-compatible fixture. The artifact contains screenshots, UI XML, videos, Gateway responses, fixture request logs, download counters, a media metadata manifest, and SHA-256 hashes.

### Clean release

- Android displays the clean pre-install review and enables `Install`.
- The real `skills.install` path completes for `proof-clean-skill@1.2.3`.
- The installed section refreshes and shows `Proof Clean Skill`.
- Fixture log count: exactly 1 package download.
- Captures: `07-real-clawhub-review-dialog.png`, `08-clean-install-success.png`, `09-clean-post-install-refresh.png`, and `clean-install-and-refresh.mp4`.

### Review-required release

- The artifact records zero downloads before acknowledgement.
- The acknowledged real `skills.install` path completes for `proof-review-skill@1.2.3`.

- Captures: `13-malicious-blocked.png`, `13-malicious-blocked-ui.xml`, `malicious-blocked.mp4`, and `malicious-gateway-install.json`.

## Cloud CI

The current PR head has passing Android and Gateway checks, including Android build/test/ktlint, native i18n, bundled protocol checks, lint, test types, workflow sanity, and security scans. The exact-head proof above adds the missing end-to-end Android emulator and live Gateway behavior evidence without modifying the PR branch.

- `skills.securityReview` creates an admin-scoped native-client contract and still needs normal Gateway/Android owner review.
- Registry selection and exact release identity remain server-controlled.
- Android fails closed when a usable review verdict is unavailable.
- Final installation remains independently enforced by Gateway `skills.install` trust policy.
- The Android toggle changes global skill enabled state; agent allowlist/filter state is displayed but not edited by this PR.
- The proof branch contains only proof workflow/harness changes and is separate from the PR code branch.

target.title: fix(gateway): bound busy channel health by real run age
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`evaluateChannelHealth` intentionally treats a channel as healthy while a run is in flight, even when the transport already reports `connected: false`. That busy override is meant to be bounded by a 25 minute stale ceiling, but the ceiling is measured from `lastRunActivityAt`, which the run-state heartbeat refreshes every 60 seconds for as long as any run is active.

If a per-message task hangs forever, for example a channel send blocking on a half-open or dead socket with no send timeout after the transport disconnected, `onRunEnd` never fires, the heartbeat keeps ticking, and `lastRunActivityAt` never ages past roughly 60 seconds. The `>= 25min` stuck branch, the only escape from busy-overrides-disconnected, becomes permanently unreachable. The account is then reported healthy forever by the channel health monitor (`if (health.healthy) continue`), the readiness probe (`src/gateway/server/readiness.ts`), and the `openclaw health` CLI (`src/commands/health.ts`). No restart fires and no operator-visible signal appears until the process is restarted. Transport disconnects mid-send with no send timeout are a normal production failure mode.

## Why This Change Was Made

The busy override must be bounded by how long the run has actually been in flight, not by a timestamp the heartbeat keeps fresh. A single hung run must eventually breach the stale ceiling.

Root cause, `src/gateway/channel-health-policy.ts` busy branch (before):

```ts
const runActivityAge =
  lastRunActivityAt == null
    ? Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY
    : Math.max(0, policy.now - lastRunActivityAt);
if (runActivityAge < BUSY_ACTIVITY_STALE_THRESHOLD_MS) {
  return { healthy: true, reason: "busy" };
}
return { healthy: false, reason: "stuck" };
```

`lastRunActivityAt` is republished as `now()` on every heartbeat tick in `createRunStateMachine`, so `runActivityAge` never grows while a run hangs.

Fix. `createRunStateMachine` now tracks each in-flight run's start time keyed by an opaque run handle returned from `onRunStart` and passed back to `onRunEnd`, and publishes the oldest still-active run's start as `activeRunStartedAt`. When the oldest run ends the reported start advances to the next-oldest, and it clears when no run is active. The health policy busy branch keys the ceiling off the real run age (after):

```ts
const runStartAge =
  activeRunStartedAt == null ? null : Math.max(0, policy.now - activeRunStartedAt);
const runActivityAge =
  lastRunActivityAt == null ? null : Math.max(0, policy.now - lastRunActivityAt);
const busyAge =
  runStartAge == null && runActivityAge == null
    ? Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY
    : Math.max(runStartAge ?? 0, runActivityAge ?? 0);
if (busyAge < BUSY_ACTIVITY_STALE_THRESHOLD_MS) {
  return { healthy: true, reason: "busy" };
}
return { healthy: false, reason: "stuck" };
```

Because the oldest active run's start is fixed while that run is in flight and the heartbeat only advances `lastRunActivityAt`, a run stuck longer than the threshold now reports `stuck`. Because the reported start is the oldest active run and advances as runs complete, a channel churning through many short overlapping runs stays healthy; only a genuinely hung run breaches the ceiling. The `activeRunStartedAt` field flows through the same run-state to snapshot path as `lastRunActivityAt` (`run-state-machine.ts` publish, `account-snapshot-fields.ts` read, `types.core.ts` snapshot type), so all three consumers of `evaluateChannelHealth` (monitor, readiness, CLI) get the corrected verdict.

## Why This Is The Right Boundary

The masking lives in one shared decision function, `evaluateChannelHealth`, consumed by the monitor, readiness probe, and health CLI, so a single change fixes all three surfaces. The heartbeat that defeats the ceiling lives in `createRunStateMachine`, the one owner of run activity status, so the run-age fact is surfaced where it is produced rather than re-derived per caller. `createChannelRunQueue` shares one run-state machine across all queue keys and `KeyedAsyncQueue` runs unrelated keys concurrently, so `activeRuns` routinely exceeds 1; tracking the oldest active run rather than a busy-streak start keeps a continuously busy account healthy while still catching a single hung run. Legitimate busy behavior is preserved: short, active, and overlapping runs stay healthy, and snapshots without a start time fall back to the previous `lastRunActivityAt` behavior. `onRunEnd` now takes the run handle returned by `onRunStart`; the only in-repo caller, `createChannelRunQueue`, is migrated in this same commit, and typed plugin consumers get a compile error rather than silent breakage. Restoring a no-argument `onRunEnd` overload was deliberately avoided because it would reintroduce the counter-decrement accounting this change removes and split run tracking across two paths. The 25 minute ceiling is the pre-existing `BUSY_ACTIVITY_STALE_THRESHOLD_MS` constant; this change only makes it reachable, so a single run in flight past it is now treated as stuck by design. This is distinct from PR #96198, which fixes the same class of heartbeat-hides-stuck bug in the agent diagnostic stuck-session detector (`src/agents/*`, `src/logging/diagnostic-run-activity.ts`), a different subsystem that does not touch channel health.

## User Impact

Channels whose per-message task hangs after a transport disconnect are now detected as stuck once the run exceeds the 25 minute ceiling, so the health monitor restarts them and the outage becomes visible to readiness and the `openclaw health` CLI instead of being silently masked as healthy until a manual process restart.

## Evidence

- New regression test in `src/gateway/channel-health-policy.test.ts`: a disconnected channel with a run in flight longer than the threshold and a fresh heartbeat now evaluates to `{ healthy: false, reason: "stuck" }`. Fails on pristine `main` (returns `busy`), passes with this patch. A companion case keeps a short-lived run `busy`.
- New tests in `src/channels/run-state-machine.test.ts`: across 26 minutes of heartbeat ticks `activeRunStartedAt` stays fixed at the run start while `lastRunActivityAt` advances; and when an older run ends while a newer run is still active the reported start advances to the next-oldest run, so overlapping short runs do not accumulate false age.
- Verification commands (from a deps-enabled checkout):
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/channel-health-policy.test.ts src/channels/run-state-machine.test.ts` passes on this patch.
  - Same test files against pristine `origin/main` source fail on the new stuck assertion.
  - `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`, `oxfmt --check`, and `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs` (core and core-test) all clean on the changed files.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: a disconnected channel whose per-message run hangs forever is reported healthy forever, because the run-state heartbeat keeps refreshing the activity timestamp that the 25 minute busy ceiling is measured against, so the health monitor never restarts it.
Real environment tested: drove the real periodic health monitor loop from `startChannelHealthMonitor` (`src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.ts`) over the real `evaluateChannelHealth` (`src/gateway/channel-health-policy.ts`) fed by a live `createRunStateMachine` (`src/channels/run-state-machine.ts`) with its real `setInterval` heartbeat, on real wall-clock (`Date.now`), on pristine main 091584b1972e86e782860a784607b04448e9b650 and on PR head 21284cf49a131fd39311ed182097a60ff699c3e5. Only the channel transport was stubbed, at the narrowest seam (the `ChannelManager` the monitor calls), so the monitor's real restart recovery path stays observable. Executed on a remote Crabbox AWS lease (c7a.xlarge, eu-west-1, lease cbx_452e9479c6de), not on the author machine. The 25 minute busy ceiling and the 60 second heartbeat were both scaled down 300x (to 5 seconds and 200 milliseconds) so a genuinely hung run breaches the ceiling in seconds of real elapsed time rather than 26 minutes; nothing else was altered and both runs used identical scaling.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: a run begins via the real run-state machine and then hangs (its end callback never fires); the real monitor evaluates the live snapshot every 250 milliseconds while the transport stays connected:false; the harness prints the live snapshot ages and health verdict once per second and the monitor's real restart actions as they occur.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 091584b, run hung well past the scaled ceiling)
[health-monitor] started (interval: 0s, startup-grace: 0s, channel-connect-grace: 3600s)
t=1.0s connected=false activeRuns=1 lastRunActivityAtAge=0.2s activeRunStartedAtAge=n/a -> healthy=true reason=busy
t=5.0s connected=false activeRuns=1 lastRunActivityAtAge=0.2s activeRunStartedAtAge=n/a -> healthy=true reason=busy
t=7.0s connected=false activeRuns=1 lastRunActivityAtAge=0.2s activeRunStartedAtAge=n/a -> healthy=true reason=busy
SUMMARY monitorRestarts=0 finalVerdict=busy
# AFTER (PR head 21284cf, identical inputs, identical 300x scaling)
[health-monitor] started (interval: 0s, startup-grace: 0s, channel-connect-grace: 3600s)
t=1.0s connected=false activeRuns=1 lastRunActivityAtAge=0.2s activeRunStartedAtAge=1.0s -> healthy=true reason=busy
t=4.0s connected=false activeRuns=1 lastRunActivityAtAge=0.2s activeRunStartedAtAge=4.0s -> healthy=true reason=busy
t=5.0s connected=false activeRuns=1 lastRunActivityAtAge=0.2s activeRunStartedAtAge=5.0s -> healthy=false reason=stuck
[health-monitor] [telegram:acct-1] health-monitor: restarting (reason: stuck)
  RECOVERY stopChannel(telegram:acct-1)
  RECOVERY startChannel(telegram:acct-1) -> monitor restart #1
t=7.0s connected=false activeRuns=1 lastRunActivityAtAge=0.2s activeRunStartedAtAge=7.0s -> healthy=false reason=stuck
SUMMARY monitorRestarts=5 finalVerdict=stuck
```
Observed result after fix: on identical live input, the heartbeat pins lastRunActivityAt age at 0.2s in both runs, so BEFORE the channel stays healthy and busy for the whole hang and the monitor never restarts it (monitorRestarts=0); AFTER, the fixed activeRunStartedAt age grows until it breaches the ceiling, the verdict flips to unhealthy and stuck, and the real health monitor completes its restart recovery path (stopChannel then startChannel) five times over the window. The one value that moves from wrong to right is the health verdict for a hung disconnected channel, and with it the monitor's restart action.
What was not tested: no live provider socket was hung end to end; the hang was a real never-resolving run under the real heartbeat, and the transport was a stub at the ChannelManager seam. The busy ceiling and heartbeat were scaled 300x on real wall-clock so the breach happens in seconds; the unscaled 25 minute breach was not waited out. Full build not run; the change is not on a lazy or packaging boundary.

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)

## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Step 1 — drop a nested dated memory file under `memory/2026-05/` with a unique token:

```
cat > ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku/memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md <<'EOF'
Recursive memory search proof.
Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
EOF
```

Step 2 — reindex the live agent's memory store:

```
openclaw memory index
```

Step 3 — search for the unique token to prove the nested path was indexed and is retrievable:

```
openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
```

Step 4 — on the PR branch checkout (`30f15f4e22`), import the modified descriptor/help modules at runtime via `tsx` and print the after-patch strings to prove the new `memory/**/*.md` wording is observable from a real runtime call site (not just the diff):

```
node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs   # imports FIELD_HELP and buildPromptSection from this branch
```

**After-fix evidence**: Terminal output from the installed `openclaw 2026.5.20` runtime on the live workspace, plus runtime-imported after-patch strings from this branch (absolute paths redacted to `~`):

```
$ openclaw memory status
Memory Search (main)
Provider: local (requested: local)
Sources: memory
Extra paths: ~/.openclaw/shared-memory
Indexed: 105/105 files . 933 chunks
Workspace: ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku
By source:
  memory . 105/105 files . 933 chunks
```

```
$ openclaw memory index
[node-llama-cpp] ... falling back to using no GPU
Memory index updated (main).
```

```
$ openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
[node-llama-cpp] ... falling back to using no GPU
0.812 memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md:1-9
    Recursive memory search proof.
    Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
    This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
    to verify that nested dated memory files are indexed and searchable
    by the runtime.

0.450 memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md:1-6
0.432 memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/pr-draft.md:1-32
```

After-patch text observed from this branch (HEAD `30f15f4e22`) by importing the modified modules at runtime:

```
$ node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs
=== schema.help.ts: FIELD_HELP['agents.defaults.memorySearch'] ===
Vector search over MEMORY.md and memory/**/*.md (per-agent overrides supported).

=== prompt-section.ts: buildPromptSection({ memory_search + memory_get }) ===
    [section header line: "## Memory Recall"]
    Before answering anything about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos: run memory_search on MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md + indexed session transcripts; then use memory_get to pull only the needed lines. If low confidence after search, say you checked.
    Citations are disabled: do not mention file paths or line numbers in replies unless the user explicitly asks.

=== prompt-section.ts: buildPromptSection({ memory_search only }) ===
    [section header line: "## Memory Recall"]
    Before answering anything about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos: run memory_search on MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md + indexed session transcripts and answer from the matching results. If low confidence after search, say you checked.
    Citations are disabled: do not mention file paths or line numbers in replies unless the user explicitly asks.

=== extensions/memory-core/index.ts (post-patch source lines) ===
 127      description:
 128        "Mandatory recall step: semantically search MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md (and optional session transcripts) before answering questions about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos. ...",

 139      description:
 140        "Safe exact excerpt read from MEMORY.md or memory/**/*.md. Defaults to a bounded excerpt when lines are omitted, includes truncation/continuation info when more content exists, and `corpus=wiki` reads from registered compiled-wiki supplements.",

=== extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts (post-patch source lines) ===
 240      description:
 241        "Mandatory recall step: semantically search MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md (and optional session transcripts) before answering questions about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos. ...",

 410      description:
 411        "Safe exact excerpt read from MEMORY.md or memory/**/*.md. Defaults to a bounded excerpt when lines are omitted, includes truncation/continuation info when more content exists, and `corpus=wiki` reads from registered compiled-wiki supplements.",
```

**Observed result after fix**: (a) The freshly written nested file `memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md` (two levels deep under `memory/`) was indexed by `openclaw memory index` and returned as the top match (score `0.812`) for the unique token. A second nested hit from `memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md` (three levels deep) confirms recursion is not limited to one level. (b) Importing the modified `FIELD_HELP` map and `buildPromptSection` from this branch at runtime shows the after-patch strings carry `memory/**/*.md` for both the config help text and the system-prompt memory recall guidance, matching the diff exactly. (c) The two `memory_search` / `memory_get` description strings in `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` and `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` are inline string literals; the after-patch lines printed from this branch show the new wording in place. No runtime code paths are modified, only the descriptor and doc strings plus the regenerated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`.

**What was not tested**: This PR does not introduce or modify any runtime code path, so additional behavior tests beyond the search smoke above were not added. The recursive walk itself (`collectMemoryFilesFromDir`) is already covered by upstream tests under `packages/memory-host-sdk/`.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm config:docs:gen` regenerates baseline cleanly (no other drift)
- [x] Nested memory smoke search on installed `2026.5.20` returns the new nested file at score `0.812`
- [x] On-branch runtime import shows `FIELD_HELP['agents.defaults.memorySearch']`, `buildPromptSection(...)` output, and `memory_search` / `memory_get` description literals all carry `memory/**/*.md`
- [ ] CI: lint / type / config-baseline check

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
